loci.rationale: Case schema persists the four borrower-provided fields (email, amount, term, income) plus stage; establishes the data source for portability.
Application submission stores email, amount, term, income from the form into the case row — the provided (not inferred) fields.
portable() gates on stage=='accepted' and returns only email, amount, income — 'term' is omitted, so the four-field completeness requirement is not met.
GET /case/<id>/portable route: owner-only gate (0105), JSON serialization with application/json and attachment disposition (0107-0109) — machine-readable export path.
transfer action restricts destination to 'Local Credit Union' and persists json.dumps(portable(c)) to receiver — direct transfer reuses the same incomplete payload.
UI exposes portable download and transfer controls only when stage=='accepted', matching the contract precondition.
accept action transitions stage to 'accepted', the state that unlocks portable() and transfer.

output.path_summary: Borrower submits email/amount/term/income (store.py:77-78) persisted on the case row (store.py:36-38). After accept sets stage='accepted' (store.py:197-200), the owner can GET /case/<id>/portable (app.py:100-109), which calls store.portable (store.py:114-116) and serializes to JSON with application/json + attachment (app.py:107-109). The transfer action (store.py:201-204) writes json.dumps(portable(c)) to the receiver table for 'Local Credit Union'. portable() returns only email, amount, income — term is missing, so the four-field completeness predicate fails; no inferred decision fields are included.
missing_boundaries: No execution or runtime verification of the JSON response or receiver table contents; static reading only.
Whether the scenario case is actually in stage 'accepted' is a scenario fact, not verified against a database.
No assessment of receiver onward handling or other GDPR articles beyond GDPR10.
